conclusion: EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037-7043; read once in full from the held FR text) revokes EO 13766, 13778, 13783, 13792, 13795, 13868 and 13927 in one sentence of sec. 7(a) ('are hereby revoked'), partly revokes EO 13834, revokes EO 13807 in sec. 7(b), suspends EO 13920 for 90 days and revokes three Presidential memoranda in sec. 7(d). It states no effective date and has no delayed-effect wording, so every revocation took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Sec. 7(f) orders the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind the orders, rules and policies that implement or enforce the revoked instruments, so the order is built to remove implementing residue, not to preserve it. Sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and does not save any revoked order, right or pending action. Sec. 8(c) disclaims private rights. The order transfers no function from the revoked orders to anyone else; sec. 7(b) only asks OMB and CEQ to consider a replacement for EO 13807. One interaction matters for EO 13795: sec. 4(b) says EO 13754 and the Presidential Memorandum of December 20, 2016 were revoked/amended by EO 13795 and 'are hereby reinstated in their original form'. It reinstates only those two instruments. EO 13795 sec. 5 also modified the withdrawal memoranda of January 27, 2015 and July 14, 2008; sec. 4(b) of EO 13990 does not reach them, so that part of EO 13795's own effect is not undone by the revocation list. For the other five orders in this batch the reading finds no surviving own effect; the S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) is consistent for them and is overruled for EO 13795 only after the order itself is read.
